title: Remarketing Rule: Sale of a Repossessed Vehicle, Surplus and Deficiency on the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Remarketing rule, Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

1. A repossessed vehicle can be sold only while the contract status is repossessed.
2. **Notice period.** The sale may take place no earlier than the product's company minimum period after the notice of intent to sell was mailed. The period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the notice mailing date; where the contract records a state minimum notice period longer than the company minimum, that longer period is used in the same count, and a sale on the first day after the period is permitted.
3. **Proceeds.** Net proceeds are gross proceeds less sale expenses and are applied to principal; the contract moves to deficiency when the principal balance plus the fees-due balance remains above zero, and to paid in full when the net proceeds cover it.
4. **Surplus.** A surplus is refunded to the customer within the product's surplus refund period in calendar days of the sale together with a surplus notice.
5. **Settlement.** A deficiency balance may be settled for a lump sum of at least the product's minimum settlement percentage of the deficiency, which pays the contract in full; a smaller offer is not within the servicing desk's authority.
6. **Charge-off.** A deficiency can be charged off only while the contract status is deficiency. A deficiency may be charged off no earlier than the product's charge-off period after the vehicle was sold. The period is counted in calendar days starting the day after the scheduled sale date, and charge-off on the last day of the period is permitted.

## Time tests

| Test | Clock starts | Earliest permitted day |
|---|---|---|
| Sale after the notice | the day after the notice mailing date | the first day after the period (company minimum, or the longer recorded state period) |
| Charge-off after the sale | the day after the scheduled sale date | the last day of the charge-off period |

*Boundary cases (abstract):* with a notice period of N days, a sale on day N after the mailing date is not permitted and a sale on day N plus 1 is; with a charge-off period of C days, charge-off on day C after the sale is permitted and on day C less 1 is not.

*Hypothetical proceeds:* gross proceeds of 18,000.00 dollars and sale expenses of 1,200.00 dollars give net proceeds of 16,800.00 dollars, applied to principal; if the principal balance plus fees due was 20,000.00 dollars, 3,200.00 dollars remains and the contract moves to deficiency.
